[Switching from r-help to ggplot list as this is of more interest to the
specialized audience.]

On 7/15/2011 10:01 AM, Hadley Wickham wrote:
>> You should only have one scale_ call for each scale type. Here, you have
>> three scale_colour_ calls, the first selecting a grey scale, the second
>> defining a single break with its label (and thus implicitly subsetting on
>> that single break value), and a second which defines a different
>> break/label/subset. Only the last one has any effect.
>
> Just to clarify: breaks/labels control the appearance of the
> legend/axis, limits modify what data is shown on the plot.
>
> Hadley

You are right. I got thrown off by the behavior of scale_colour_grey:

pcd <- qplot(cyl, mpg, colour=factor(cyl), data=mtcars)
pcd
pcd + scale_colour_grey()
pcd + scale_colour_grey(breaks=c("6","8"), label=c("six","eight"))
pcd + scale_colour_grey(breaks=c("6"), label=c("six"))


The last three all use scale_colour_grey, but with different breaks.
However, different breaks lead to different mappings to shades of grey.
Specifically, if breaks is of length n, only the first n levels of the
variable are given a grey color (spread over the range of the n points);
all others are given (? NA?). That's what confused me into thinking
they were being dropped. They are not, as these examples show. But they
are not being plotted, either.

Should not scale_grey distribute the scale over all possible values of
the aesthetic variable, and only label in the legend those listed in breaks?

This behavior is not present in the devel version; in the devel branch,
the mapping between factor(cyl) and grey level is the same independent
of the breaks specified. So I suppose this is just a note that this is
a problem in 0.8.9.
